log.why: Testing the leading candidate dnaK (0.395) gives a high chance of confirming it in a single plate, while rejecting it narrows down the remaining genes.
Treating at 10 uM bisects the dose probability mass while Ticket 1's plate incubates.
E3 (3 µM) splits the remaining posterior mass nearly in half (0.572 vs 0.428) while we prepare to publish Ticket 1.
Test {gyrA, recA} on Ticket 3 to split the prior probability nearly in half while incubators are free.
Test 1 µM on Ticket 2 to distinguish 3 µM from lower thresholds while incubators are free before publishing Ticket 1.
Posterior for dnaK is 0.880 after only one plate, giving high expected points and freeing capacity.
Test gyrA directly to distinguish between the two top candidates, gyrA and recA, which share 91% of the posterior.
Ticket 2 has a strong 0.793 posterior for 3 uM and only 36s left; publishing now secures high points.
Test {lacZ, sodA} (combined posterior 0.476) to split the probability mass evenly while incubators are free, before publishing Ticket 3.
gyrA has a 0.904 posterior after two positive knockout tests, making it ready to publish.
Test sodA directly to distinguish between the two leading candidates, sodA (0.496) and lacZ (0.415), before Ticket 4 expires.
E3 bisects the dose threshold prior (0.632 <= 3 uM vs 0.368 > 3 uM) while we wait for Ticket 4's plate.
Ticket 4 has only 11 seconds left and lacZ has a strong posterior of 0.744.
E4 tests whether the threshold is at most 10 uM, strongly separating the leading 10 uM hypothesis from higher doses.
Test top candidate fliC on Ticket 8 while waiting for Ticket 5's E4 plate to finish.
With only 7 seconds left in the round, no new plates can finish, and Ticket 5 has a strong positive expected value at 0.551 posterior.
Only 1 second remains in the round, so no experiment or publication can finish before time expires.
